title: Why subtitles matter
paragraphs: Over half of American TV viewers now use subtitles whenever they watch TV, according to survey company YouGov. This trend is even more noticeable in viewers under 30. Subtitles have long been used to help people with hearing impairments or to allow people to watch films in a different language, but why has their use become so widespread?

The reasons for this are both technical and social. Advances in digital sound production and microphones mean that actors can be more natural in their vocal performance, while at the same time audio directors are able to make more and more dramatic soundscapes. Combined with the much smaller speakers contained in modern TV sets, this can all make dialogue seem unintelligible. Smartphones may play a role. We are used to subtitled social media videos that can be watched without headphones. Smartphones also allow us to watch film and TV in public places where they are not easily audible. Another social reason could be the increased appetite for programmes in other languages accessible through international streaming services.

While some viewers may consider subtitles to be distracting, or worry about the potential for spoilers, they don't just help with unclear audio. A number of studies have suggested that subtitles could help people to increase their vocabulary and boost their listening skills in languages that they do not currently speak.

This may be particularly effective when subtitles are in the same language as the audio track of the programme. Same-language subtitles have also been shown to help young children develop their reading skills in their first language, to the point where campaigners have suggested enabling subtitles on all children's programmes by default.

vocabulary.example: The film has English subtitles for non-native speakers.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影为非母语观众提供了英文字幕。

vocabulary.example: There's a growing trend towards working from home.
vocabulary.translation: 在家工作的趋势日益增长。

vocabulary.entry: **noticeable** /ˈnəʊtɪsəbl/ adj. 显著的，显而易见的
vocabulary.example: There has been a noticeable improvement in her work.
vocabulary.translation: 她的工作有了显著的进步。

vocabulary.example: The condition can cause severe visual impairment.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病可能导致严重的视力损伤。

vocabulary.example: Recent advances in medical science have saved many lives.
vocabulary.translation: 医学科学的最新进展挽救了许多生命。

vocabulary.example: He spoke into the microphone so the audience could hear him.
vocabulary.translation: 他对着麦克风讲话，以便观众能听到他的声音。

vocabulary.example: She has a great vocal range.
vocabulary.translation: 她的音域很广。

vocabulary.example: There has been a dramatic change in the weather.
vocabulary.translation: 天气发生了戏剧性的变化。

vocabulary.example: The soundscape of the city includes traffic noise and sirens.
vocabulary.translation: 城市的声景包括交通噪音和警笛声。

vocabulary.example: The phone has a built-in speaker.
vocabulary.translation: 这部手机有一个内置扬声器。

vocabulary.entry: **unintelligible** /ˌʌnɪnˈtelɪdʒəbl/ adj. 难以理解的，听不清的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The speech was almost unintelligible.
vocabulary.translation: 这演讲几乎听不清楚。

vocabulary.example: His voice was barely audible above the noise.
vocabulary.translation: 在嘈杂声中，他的声音几乎听不见。

vocabulary.example: The public has an insatiable appetite for celebrity gossip.
vocabulary.translation: 公众对名人八卦有着永不满足的欲望。

vocabulary.entry: **accessible** /əkˈsesəbl/ adj. 可获得的，可访问的
vocabulary.example: The website is accessible to all users.
vocabulary.translation: 所有用户都可以访问该网站。

vocabulary.entry: **distracting** /dɪˈstræktɪŋ/ adj. 令人分心的，分散注意力的
vocabulary.example: The noise from the street was very distracting.
vocabulary.translation: 街上的噪音非常让人分心。

vocabulary.example: The review contains spoilers for the film's ending.
vocabulary.translation: 这篇评论包含了电影结局的剧透。

vocabulary.example: Reading widely helps to increase your vocabulary.
vocabulary.translation: 广泛阅读有助于增加词汇量。

vocabulary.example: Winning the competition boosted her confidence.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得比赛增强了她的信心。

vocabulary.entry: **audio track** /ˈɔːdiəʊ træk/ n. 音轨，声音轨道（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The film has a commentary track and the original audio track.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影有一条评论音轨和原始音轨。

vocabulary.entry: **campaigner** /kæmˈpeɪnə(r)/ n. 活动家，运动参与者（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Campaigners are calling for stricter gun control laws.
vocabulary.translation: 活动人士呼吁实行更严格的枪支管制法律。

vocabulary.example: The new software enables users to edit videos easily.
vocabulary.translation: 新软件使用户能够轻松编辑视频。

vocabulary.entry: **by default** /baɪ dɪˈfɔːlt/ phr. 默认情况下（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The settings are enabled by default.
vocabulary.translation: 这些设置默认是启用的。

vocabulary.example: The movie has some very funny dialogue.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影有一些非常有趣的对话。

vocabulary.entry: **streaming service** /ˈstriːmɪŋ ˌsɜːvɪs/ n. 流媒体服务（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Many people now use streaming services instead of buying CDs.
vocabulary.translation: 现在许多人使用流媒体服务而不是购买CD。

vocabulary.example: She listened to music on her headphones.
vocabulary.translation: 她戴着耳机听音乐。

sentences.english: Over half of American TV viewers now use subtitles whenever they watch TV, according to survey company YouGov.
sentences.chinese: 根据调查公司YouGov的数据，超过一半的美国电视观众现在看电视时都会使用字幕。

sentences.english: This trend is even more noticeable in viewers under 30.
sentences.chinese: 这种趋势在30岁以下的观众中更为明显。

sentences.english: Subtitles have long been used to help people with hearing impairments or to allow people to watch films in a different language, but why has their use become so widespread?
sentences.chinese: 长期以来，字幕一直用于帮助有听力障碍的人，或者让人们观看不同语言的电影，但为什么字幕的使用变得如此普遍呢？

sentences.english: The reasons for this are both technical and social.
sentences.chinese: 其原因既有技术方面的，也有社会方面的。

sentences.english: Advances in digital sound production and microphones mean that actors can be more natural in their vocal performance, while at the same time audio directors are able to make more and more dramatic soundscapes.
sentences.chinese: 数字声音制作和麦克风的进步意味着演员可以更自然地进行声音表演，同时音频导演能够制作出越来越戏剧化的声景。

sentences.english: Combined with the much smaller speakers contained in modern TV sets, this can all make dialogue seem unintelligible.
sentences.chinese: 再加上现代电视机中内置的扬声器尺寸小得多，所有这些都可能导致对话听起来难以理解。
智能手机可能也起到了一定作用。

sentences.english: We are used to subtitled social media videos that can be watched without headphones.
sentences.chinese: 我们已经习惯了无需耳机即可观看的带字幕的社交媒体视频。

sentences.english: Smartphones also allow us to watch film and TV in public places where they are not easily audible.
sentences.chinese: 智能手机还让我们可以在公共场所观看电影和电视节目，而在这些地方声音不易听清。

sentences.english: Another social reason could be the increased appetite for programmes in other languages accessible through international streaming services.
sentences.chinese: 另一个社会原因可能是，通过国际流媒体服务可以获取的其他语言的节目需求增加了。

sentences.english: While some viewers may consider subtitles to be distracting, or worry about the potential for spoilers, they don't just help with unclear audio.
sentences.chinese: 虽然有些观众可能认为字幕会分散注意力，或者担心有剧透的可能，但字幕不仅仅有助于解决音频不清楚的问题。

sentences.english: A number of studies have suggested that subtitles could help people to increase their vocabulary and boost their listening skills in languages that they do not currently speak.
sentences.chinese: 许多研究表明，字幕可以帮助人们增加词汇量，并提高他们目前不熟悉语言的听力技能。

sentences.english: This may be particularly effective when subtitles are in the same language as the audio track of the programme.
sentences.chinese: 当字幕与节目的音轨使用同一种语言时，这可能尤其有效。

sentences.english: Same-language subtitles have also been shown to help young children develop their reading skills in their first language, to the point where campaigners have suggested enabling subtitles on all children's programmes by default.
sentences.chinese: 同语言字幕也被证明有助于幼儿发展他们的母语阅读能力，以至于支持者们建议在所有儿童节目中默认开启字幕。
